How to Sync Viewers with mast-aladin and jdaviz#

Learning Goals#

This is a beginner tutorial on synchronizing the viewer state between mast-aladin and jdaviz viewers. By the end of this tutorial, you will:

  • Understand what a viewer’s viewport represents.

  • Be able to sync viewport properties using the Viewer Sync UI.

Table of Contents#

  • What is a Viewport?

  • Imports

  • Widget Setup

    • Initialize widgets

    • Display widgets

    • Register widgets

  • Viewer Sync UI

  • Exercise

What is a Viewport?#

A viewport is the part of an image currently visible in a viewer. Both jdaviz and mast-aladin implement the Astro Image Display API (AIDA), which describes a viewport using properties such as its sky-coordinate center, field of view, rotation, and projection.

In this tutorial, we’ll sync the following viewport properties:

  • Center: The center of the viewport in sky coordinates.

  • FOV: The field of view of the viewport, measured along the viewer’s shorter side.

  • Rotation: The rotation applied to the image in the viewport

  • Projection: The current projection applied to the viewport

Imports#

We will import the following in this tutorial:

  • mast-aladin: to create sky viewers and manage synchronization.

  • jdaviz: to create an image viewer.

  • Sidecar: to arrange the viewers in the notebook.

import jdaviz as jd

from mast_aladin import MastAladin, MastManager

from sidecar import Sidecar

Widget Setup#

Initialize widgets: Before syncing viewers, we’ll create two mast-aladin viewers and one jdaviz viewer. We’ll point them at the Cartwheel Galaxy so their views can be compared.

  • mast_aladin: loads the Cartwheel Galaxy.

  • mast_aladin_2mass: loads the Cartwheel Galaxy using the 2MASS survey.

  • jdaviz: loads a JWST NIRCam image of the Cartwheel Galaxy.

mast_aladin = MastAladin(
    target="Cartwheel Galaxy",
    fov=1,
    height=500
)

mast_aladin_2mass = MastAladin(
    target="Cartwheel Galaxy",
    fov=1,
    height=500,
    survey='https://alaskybis.cds.unistra.fr/2MASS/Color/'
)

uri = 'mast:JWST/product/jw02727-o002_t062_nircam_clear-f090w_i2d.fits'
jdaviz = jd.App()
jdaviz.load(uri, format="Image", cache=True)

Downloading URL https://mast.stsci.edu/api/v0.1/Download/file?uri=mast:JWST/product/jw02727-o002_t062_nircam_clear-f090w_i2d.fits to ./jw02727-o002_t062_nircam_clear-f090w_i2d.fits ...

 [Done]

Display widgets: We’ll place each viewer in a sidecar so the views remain visible while you use the sync controls. Run the cell below to display the jdaviz app and both mast-aladin viewers. For more information on how this is done, please see the how to organize widgets tutorial.

# Create a sidecar
jdaviz_sc = Sidecar(title="jdaviz", anchor="split-right")
with jdaviz_sc:
    jdaviz.show()

# Create a sidecar with defined anchor
mast_aladin_sc = Sidecar(title="mast_aladin", ref=jdaviz_sc, anchor="split-bottom")

with mast_aladin_sc:
    display(mast_aladin)

mast_aladin_2mass_sc = Sidecar(title="mast_aladin_2mass", ref=mast_aladin_sc, anchor="split-right")
with mast_aladin_2mass_sc:
    display(mast_aladin_2mass)

Register widgets: Next, we’ll register all three viewers with MastManager. This lets the Viewer Sync UI list them as possible sources and destinations.

mm = MastManager()

mm.register_app(mast_aladin, "mast_aladin")
mm.register_app(mast_aladin_2mass, "mast_aladin_2mass")
mm.register_app(jdaviz, "jdaviz")

Viewer Sync UI#

The viewers are registered and visible. Run the cell below to open the Viewer Sync UI, then choose:

  • Source: The widget whose viewport changes will be shared.

  • Destinations: One or more widgets that receive those updates.

  • Aspects: Center, Field of View, Rotation, and Projection.

mm.display_plugin("viewer_sync")

Exercise#

Set mast_aladin as the source and mast_aladin_2mass and jdaviz as destinations. Enable the viewport properties needed to reproduce the example below. Compare the viewers with the screenshot when you’re done.
